mechanism: An agent learns a compressed spatial (VAE) and temporal (RNN/MDN) representation of its environment unsupervised, forming a 'world model'. A small controller (C) uses latent features from this world model—rather than raw observations—to select actions. The world model predicts future latent states, allowing the controller to be trained entirely inside hallucinated 'dream' rollouts generated by the model, with the resulting policy then transferred back to the real environment.
invariant: The separation of representational learning (V+M components) from policy learning (C component) remains constant: the world model is always trained unsupervised on environment observations, and the controller always operates on compressed latent features rather than raw sensory input, regardless of the specific RL environment.
prediction: A policy trained solely inside the agent's hallucinated dream environment (world model rollouts) will transfer and perform competitively in the real environment, because the world model captures sufficient structure of the true environment dynamics.
failure_mode: If the world model is inaccurate or biased—e.g., it fails to capture rare but critical environment dynamics—the agent can exploit model errors ('hallucination artifacts') to achieve high dream-world reward without learning a policy that generalizes to the real environment.
source_excerpt: We can even train our agent entirely inside of its own hallucinated dream generated by its world model, and transfer this policy back into the actual environment. [...] By using features extracted from the world model as inputs to an agent, we can train a very compact and simple policy that can solve the required task.
